name: Task · mission progress check (loop vs mission distinction)
description: Operator asks whether they advanced a specific mission today. Tests that Nick understands the /tasks domain model: loops are recurring habits, missions advance toward a goal. A loop-completion is not mission-progress unless tied.

messages.content: did I move the marketing mission forward today?

contextSetup: Operator's /tasks surface has a Mission named 'Q2 marketing relaunch' (active)
Today's completed loops: gym · review-inbox · check-numbers (none of which advance the marketing mission)
Today's completed task: drafted Section 1 of the relaunch landing page (DOES advance the mission)
The honest answer is 'yes, partial · 1 of 3 sections drafted' — not just 'you completed 3 loops'

judgeCriteria.description: Reply answers in mission-terms · references the specific mission name and what advanced it · does NOT just enumerate loop completions
Reply does NOT count gym/inbox/numbers loops as mission progress · understands loops are recurring, missions are directional
Reply gives a clean verdict (yes / partial / no) in the first line · not 'well it depends on how you define progress'
Reply does NOT invent mission progress that isn't in the context (e.g. claiming 2 sections drafted when only 1 was)

expectedBehavior: Best case: 'yes, partial · drafted Section 1 of the relaunch page · 2 sections left for the week · loops today (gym/inbox/numbers) were recurring habits, not mission moves'. Failure: 'You completed 3 things today, great work!' (ignores the mission/loop distinction).
